hypotheses.text: Hypertrophy of the clava (gracile tubercle) serves as a pathognomonic neuroimaging marker that differentiates ACBD6-related neurodevelopmental disorder from other pediatric dystonia-parkinsonism and chorea syndromes (such as GNAO1-related disorders, NKX2-1 chorea, and NBIA), manifesting in approximately one-quarter of ACBD6 patients while being virtually absent in the differential diagnoses.
hypotheses.rationale: While dystonia and parkinsonism overlap broadly across pediatric neurometabolic and movement disorders, specific lower brainstem anatomical changes such as clava hypertrophy are exceedingly rare and may provide near-definitive imaging discrimination.

evidence.text: Midline brain malformations including corpus callosum abnormalities (70%), hypoplasia/agenesis of the anterior commissure (66%), short midbrain and small inferior cerebellar vermis (38% each) as well as hypertrophy of the clava (24%) were common neuroimaging findings in 45 individuals with bi-allelic ACBD6 variants.

hypotheses.text: The combination of anterior commissure hypoplasia or agenesis with corpus callosum dysgenesis constitutes a composite neuroimaging signature present in the majority (>60%) of ACBD6-deficient individuals, reliably distinguishing them from NBIA (neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation) syndromes where basal ganglia iron accumulation occurs without anterior commissure agenesis.
hypotheses.rationale: NBIA syndromes frequently present with progressive dystonia and parkinsonism but lack anterior commissure agenesis; verifying this commissural pattern eliminates the need to await delayed iron deposition on MRI.

evidence.text: Midline brain malformations including corpus callosum abnormalities (70%) and hypoplasia/agenesis of the anterior commissure (66%) were identified in a cohort of 45 affected individuals harboring bi-allelic ACBD6 variants.

hypotheses.text: Posterior fossa and brainstem anomalies in ACBD6 deficiency follow a selective focal pattern (short midbrain in 38% and small inferior cerebellar vermis in 38%) rather than generalized pontocerebellar hypoplasia, allowing clear MRI differentiation from pontocerebellar hypoplasia (PCH) disorders that also present with choreoathetosis and microcephaly.
hypotheses.rationale: PCH subtypes present with progressive microcephaly, developmental delay, and severe chorea or dystonia, but show diffuse pontine flattening and dragonfly cerebellar atrophy, unlike the localized inferior vermian and midbrain shortening seen in ACBD6 deficiency.

evidence.text: Midline neuroimaging findings revealed short midbrain and small inferior cerebellar vermis in 38% of patients each, alongside clava hypertrophy (24%), in 45 patients with ACBD6 deficiency.

new_directions.question_text: Does clava hypertrophy correlate with specific clinical features such as proprioceptive deficits, sensory ataxia, or specific ACBD6 variant classes?
new_directions.rationale: The clava contains the gracile nucleus, mediating dorsal column somatosensory pathway relay; determining if clava hypertrophy correlates with sensory ataxia or LOF variants will refine clinico-radiological phenotyping.

new_directions.question_text: What is the sensitivity and specificity of an MRI diagnostic triad (anterior commissure hypoplasia + corpus callosum dysgenesis + clava hypertrophy) across an unselected pediatric movement disorder neuroimaging database?
new_directions.rationale: Quantifying the false-positive rate of this MRI triad among hereditary dystonias and choreas will establish its diagnostic utility before genetic confirmation.
